4. A native failure of a uniform perturbative log-normalizer disk

The early-time preparation boundary creates a specific analytic difficulty.

Take two adjacent qubits,  $\gamma=1$ , input  $|00\rangle$ , computational measurement, and

 $\mathcal D=\frac{\mathcal R_{11}-\mathrm{Id}}2,
\qquad
\mathcal R_{11}(X)=|11\rangle\langle11|\operatorname{Tr}X.$ This is an allowed rational GKLS generator with diamond norm at most one. Set  $H=0$ , which is allowed under every upper strength bound.

Writing  $\lambda_{\rm r}=\eta/2$ , the exact probability of output  $11$  is

 $p_\eta(t)=
e^{-\lambda_{\rm r}t}
\left(\frac{1-e^{-t}}2\right)^2
+
\int_0^t
\lambda_{\rm r}e^{-\lambda_{\rm r}s}
\left(\frac{1+e^{-s}}2\right)^2ds. \tag{14}$ At  $\eta=0$ ,

 $p_0(t)=\frac{(1-e^{-t})^2}{4}>0.$ Use negative  $\eta$  only for analytic continuation. For  $0<t\le1/4$ ,

 $p_{-t}(t)
\le t^2\left(\frac{e^{t^2/2}}4-\frac{e^{-t}}2\right)
\le-\frac{29}{248}t^2<0.$ Hence there is a real zero

 $\eta_t\in(-t,0),
\qquad
\eta_t=-\frac t2+O(t^2).$ Therefore the Taylor series at  $\eta=0$  of

 $\log\frac{p_\eta(t)}{p_0(t)}$ cannot have a positive convergence radius uniform over all allowed early times and pins. Its first normalized derivative is already  $2/t+O(1)$ .

This refutes that particular uniform analytic premise. It does not refute sampling. The example has an explicit four-outcome law, and independent products of these pairs have polynomial-bit samplers. Local exact resummation repairs this family. The issue is the use of a single  $\eta=0$ -centred logarithmic disk for every rare pin.
